page: Google Cloud Platform c4n-highmem-16 is an x86_64 server instance belonging to the Network Optimized family, configured with 16 dedicated virtual CPUs and 124 GB of system memory. Designed for environments requiring substantial memory headroom per compute unit, this instance provides approximately 7.75 GB of RAM per vCPU. It does not include dedicated graphics accelerators, operating with zero GPUs, and relies strictly on external network-attached storage architectures as no local storage is bundled.

Hardware allocation is dedicated, eliminating CPU resource contention typically found in shared-core or burstable configurations. Because local storage is absent and zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses are assigned by default, network throughput and remote block storage integration are critical architectural considerations for this tier. The hardware allocation delivers a cost-efficient footprint for memory-demanding deployments that do not justify specialized accelerator hardware.

Given its memory-heavy profile and dedicated compute allocation, the c4n-highmem-16 instance is well configured for in-memory caching systems, distributed memory caches, medium-scale relational and NoSQL database servers, memory-intensive data processing pipelines, and enterprise application backends requiring consistent memory availability.
